main_text.p: Videte quid vos faciatis: non enim ho-mini iudicabitis, sed Iehouae: & erituo-bifcum in negocio iudicij.2.Chron.19.6.

5. Sic tamen fit animatus, ut nec recte iudicantium applaufu, ceu vento fecun-do fublatus, nimium sibi placeat: nec eo destitutus, sibi nimium displiceat: nec iu-stam reprehensionem oderit: nec iniu-stam, plane sibi infrugiferam ducat: nec denique assentatorum fumos sibi caligi-nem in iudicando offundere, & impone-re patiatur.

Nihil dubium eft, Dauidi non medio-cri in rebus afflictis folatio fuiffe illud e-logium: Certò facturus est Iehouah Do-mino meo domum stabilem, quia praelia Iehouae Dominus meus praeliatus est, & malicia nō inuēta fuit in te à diebus tuis. 1.Sam.25.28.

Idem bene sibi conscius, praeiudicijs ꝓ-mulorum, in gratiam Saulis sub quodam iuris praetextu ipsum condemnantium, oppofuit ἀπολογίαν [?]: Num vere, & congregatio, iusticiam loquimini, aequitates iu-dicatis filij hominum? Psal.58.1. Nec erat cur sibi licet calamitoso displiceret, qui hominum praeiudicio circumuentus, bo-na con-

page.notes: Greek word "ἀπολογίαν" in the third line of the fourth paragraph is doubtful; the accent and final letters are hard to make out. Reading "ꝓ-mulorum" is also uncertain. The scan is slightly blurred at the bottom right, so "bona con-" is the last printed line with the hyphen kept as printed. The paragraph number "5." is printed in the text and was kept.
